loop.top3_why: The weighted:inverse_error strategy on a pruned low‑correlation pool (pool4) yields a stable per‑window performance (all ~0.70) and a validation score close to the leader while avoiding the high variance seen in the DBA approach. Given the unstable model ranking and correlated errors, a robust weighted combination is preferable to a deterministic mean or a DTW barycenter that can over‑fit to a single window.
loop.top3_why_not: B uses a plain mean over the full pool, which is less robust to correlated model errors and shows slightly higher overall error. C, although the lowest mean validation score, has large per‑window swings (0.625–0.753) indicating over‑fitting to one window; its DTW barycenter is sensitive to outliers in this noisy, medium‑predictability series. Thus A offers the best trade‑off between stability and accuracy.
